# dsh-obsidian-memory
Store your agent's memory as plain Markdown in an Obsidian vault.
Every memory is a `.md` file with YAML frontmatter that Obsidian indexes natively — so you can read,
edit, link and back up your agent's memory with tools you already use. Nothing is locked in a datab
t, link and back up your agent's memory with tools you already use. Nothing is locked in a database.
> **Status:** early but working. Host half (7 tools, 8 routes), sidebar panel, BM25 recall, decay/ar
chiving and GitHub sync are all implemented and verified on DSH `0.2.1-rc.5`.
## What it does
- **A sidebar panel** — click the brain icon, browse memories, filter by tag, sort by recency or imp

ortance, read and edit in place.
- **7 agent tools** — the model writes and reads its own memory wit

hout being told to.
- **Recall with a token budget** — three detail tiers (tiny / compact / detailed
) pick preview length and keyword count so recall costs what you can afford, not what the vault weig

hs.
- **BM25 ranking, no embeddings** — works offline, needs no API key, no vector store, no model c

all. CJK bigram tokenization so Chinese queries work.
- **Decay and archiving** — old, unimportant,

unreferenced memories fade; they are moved to `Memories/.archive/`, never deleted.
- **GitHub sync**
— pushes changed notes through the Contents API so another machine can pull them back. Optional, of

f unless configured.
- **Secrets are refused, not redacted** — a note containing a token or password
is skipped with a reason, because a redacted memory looks complete while being wrong.

### Manual install
If you would rather read the code before installing it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package has no runtime dependencies of its own. Everything it imports — `@deepseek-ai/schemaster
y`, `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, the client UI packages — comes from the DSH host and is declared as a pee
k-ai/cordis`, the client UI packages — comes from the DSH host and is declared as a peer dependency.
### Requirements
- **DSH** `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`. Declared as a peer range, so a mismatched host fails at install t

ime instead of misbehaving later.
- **`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`** `^3.18.0` — ships with DSH, so yo

u normally do not install it yourself.
- **Obsidian** — optional but that is the point. If Obsidian
is installed, the vault is discovered from `%APPDATA%\obsidian\obsidian.json` (Windows) or `~/.confi
g/obsidian/obsidian.json` (Linux/macOS), preferring the vault currently open. You can also set `vaul
n.json` (Linux/macOS), preferring the vault currently open. You can also set `vaultPath` explicitly.
## Configuration
All settings live in the plugin's Config schema, so they show up in DSH's own settings UI. Every fie
ld has a default; an empty config is valid.
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `vaultPath` | `""` | Absolute path to the vault. Empty = auto-discover from Obsidian. |
| `folder`

| `"Memories"` | Subfolder for memory notes, relative to the vault root. |
| `maxNoteBytes` | `2621

44` | Notes longer than this are truncated (hard cap; raising it has no effect). |
| `repo` | `""` |

`owner/name` to sync to. Empty = no sync. |
| `branch` | `"main"` | Branch to push to. |
| `tokenFi

le` | `""` | File holding a GitHub token. Empty = `~/.dsh/dsh-obsidian-memory/token`. |
| `denyFile`

| `""` | Secret blacklist, one literal per line. Empty = `~/.dsh/dsh-obsidian-memory/deny.txt`. |
|

`syncEnabled` | `true` | Whether the timer runs. |
| `syncMinutes` | `30` | Sync interval in minute

s (minimum 5). |
| `forgettingEnabled` | `false` | Allow decay/archive to actually write. Preview wo

rks either way. |
| `decayFactor` | `0.9` | Multiplier applied per decay pass. |
| `pruneThreshold`
| `0.15` | Below this importance, a note becomes eligible for archiving. |
### Setting up GitHub sync (optional)

1. Create a **private** repository. Memory can contain hostnames, paths and internal decisions.
2. C

reate a fine-grained token with **Contents: read and write** on that repo only.
3. Save it: `mkdir -

p ~/.dsh/dsh-obsidian-memory && printf '%s' '<token>' > ~/.dsh/dsh-obsidian-memory/token`
4. Set `re
po` to `owner/name` in the plugin config.
The token is never written into the plugin config or the repository. Sync state (a path → sha256 map
) lives in `~/.dsh/dsh-obsidian-memory/sync-state.json`, so only changed notes are pushed.
### Keeping secrets out
The plugin refuses to push a note containing a secret, and counts it under `blocked` rather than `fa
iled` — the two mean different things. Two layers:
- **Built-in patterns** (ship with the code): `github_pat_`, `gh[pousr]_`, `AKIA`, `sk-`, `BEGIN … P

RIVATE KEY`, `密码[:=是]…`.
- **Your own blacklist** at `~/.dsh/dsh-obsidian-memory/deny.txt` — one lit
eral string per line, `#` for comments. Put your own server addresses, passwords and key names here.
**This file stays on your machine and is never read into the source tree.**
## The 7 tools
| Tool | What it does |

| `obsidian_remember` | Write a new memory note. |
| `obsidian_search` | BM25 search over titles, ta

gs and bodies. |
| `obsidian_context` | Assemble recall into a token budget; returns tiny/compact/de

tailed. |
| `obsidian_read` | Read one note by vault-relative path. |
| `obsidian_update` | Edit an

existing note; keeps `id` and `createdAt`. |
| `obsidian_forget` | Preview or apply decay + archivin

g. Preview is the default. |
| `obsidian_sync` | Push changed notes to GitHub now. |
The plugin also registers a system-prompt section telling the model **when** to write memory — long-
term preferences, decisions and their reasons, pitfalls with the exact error text, machine-local fac
ts (paths and ports, never credentials) — and when not to: one-off intermediates, anything readable
from the code, casual remarks, discussions with no conclusion.
## Files it creates
